findings.title: AssignmentSource queued timestamp frozen at import time
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued shares the same timestamp (process start time). It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is stale/wrong queued metadata in to_dict/from_dict, breaking any ordering, debugging, or expiry logic that relies on creation time.

findings.title: to_dict returns non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery task
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 28, `to_dict()` uses `asdict()` and returns a raw datetime object for `queued`. That dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async()` in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable and datetime is not, so enqueueing outbound sync for any inbound-triggered assignment will fail serialization or require pickle and break cross-silo transport. Fix by serializing queued to ISO string and parsing/validating it in from_dict.

findings.title: should_sync signature change breaks existing overrides
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 382, `should_sync(self, attribute, sync_source=None)` adds a second positional argument. Any existing integration that overrides the old `def should_sync(self, attribute)` single-arg form will raise TypeError when src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py calls `should_sync('outbound_assignee', source)` with two args. Consequence is crashed outbound-sync tasks for those integrations. Needs backward-compatible *args/**kwargs handling.

findings.title: Outbound task passes assignment_source kwarg not declared in abstract
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 60, the task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`, but the abstract in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py declares `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` with no explicit assignment_source. Implementations matching the old exact signature without **kwargs will raise TypeError, retried 5 times then dropped, losing the sync. Those with **kwargs silently swallow the context. Tests mock ExampleIntegration so the mismatch is not caught. Fix by adding explicit param to the abstract and all implementers.

findings.title: Status sync cycle not actually prevented (dead parameter)
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 416, `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in the diff passes it and no `should_sync(..., source)` gate is added for the status outbound path, unlike the assignee path. Inbound status changes therefore still fan out to all integrations. Consequence is resolve/unresolve sync loops remain despite the PR goal, and the dead parameter misleads callers. Wire source through status inbound/outbound like assignee or revert the param.

findings.title: Missing test that different integration still syncs
findings.body: In tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py line 180, the new test only verifies that same-integration source suppresses outbound (`assert_not_called`). There is no test that a different linked integration still receives outbound sync, which is the intended behavior per the code comment about allowing other integrations to propagate. Consequence is a future change could over-suppress all outbound without test failure, breaking multi-integration sync.
